title: Alex Arkilanian
text: Hello and welcome! I am an ecologist, R developper, and consultant with a love for complex problem solving. Currently, I’m a PhD candidate in the Ecosystem Ecology Lab at Memorial University in St. John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada. There, I spend my days clarifying the role of dead organic matter in providing sustaining nutrition to ecosystems across time and space. Outside my PhD research I have developed novel methods to estimate the impact of barriers on fish movement. I am also passionate about R programming and open science for which I have led multiple trainings and workshops. You can read more about these activites in Research.

title: Aquatic connectivity
text:
Estimation methods
I developed novel methods to estimate the fragmentation of watersheds by aquatic barriers.
Community-level connectivity
I developed methods to quantify connectivity for a large portfolio of species.
Invasive species
Recent work showing that native connectivity restoration can be intimately linked to invasive species spread and establishment.

Spatial dynamics

Food web complexity

title: Open science
text:
R development
I am a passionate R programmer. I share knowledge. I train. I workshop.
Open science
I have been involved in multiple workshops aimed at exposing students in Ecology to the multiple facets of open science. This includes trainings on open science as a whole to introduce graduate students to these concepts. This also includes more advanced workshops aimed at evaluating how open Ecology is as a discipline and ways in which it can be improved.
